## Regressions

💭 nit  The language gate's reference rules reject correct product text with no way to excuse it, and they do not check the dates the conventions ban
- key: scripts/check-language.mjs#reference-rules-scope
- Where: scripts/check-language.mjs:38-39 (plan-reference and spec-reference run on every line, code and strings included), :54-55 (lang-exception and the vi files excuse only non-ascii-letter), :33 (the only full exemptions); CONTRIBUTING.md:21-24 and :30-31
- Why: Probe on a scratch file (node scripts/check-language.mjs, exit 1): `export const name = 'Task 1 of 3'` was flagged plan-reference and `export const plain = 'Spec 2 review'` spec-reference. A WBS fixture item or an en dictionary string with "Task 1" or "Spec 2" therefore turns gate:language red, and the only way out is to reword the data, because no marker excuses a reference rule. The other way round, `// measured on 9 Oct 2026 on the emulator, strokes 36% thinner` passed, although CONTRIBUTING.md:21 says the script checks "the banned references under Comments", and that list names dates and measurement logs (:30-31). Today 0 files hit either case (the gate is green).
- Fix: run the three reference rules on comment text only (the part of a line after `//`, `/*`, a leading `*` or `<!--`), or let `lang-exception:` excuse every rule on the next line; and either add a date rule for comments (for example `\b\d{1,2} (Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]* \d{4}\b`) or reword CONTRIBUTING.md:21 to say that dates and measurement logs are left to reviewers.
- approach-changing: no, a scope change in scanText plus one sentence

## New findings

🟡 major  gate:native mirrors the app into NATIVE_DIR with rsync --delete and never checks that folder, so a mistyped NATIVE_DIR deletes whatever lives there
- key: scripts/native-gate.mjs#native-dir-delete
- Where: scripts/native-gate.mjs:148-150 (mkdirSync, then `rsync -a --delete` with only the KEPT names of :29-41 excluded); :244 (`process.env.NATIVE_DIR ?? join(homedir(), 'metis-run/native/apps/metis')`, taken as given); :233 (sh runs rsync with the app as its cwd); CONTRIBUTING.md:227
- Why: rsync --delete removes every file of the target that the source lacks, sparing only excluded names. Measured on scratch folders with the same command shape (`rsync -a --delete --exclude=/node_modules --exclude=/ios app/ native/`, openrsync on this Mac): native/notes.md and native/precious/work.txt were deleted, native/node_modules/k.txt was kept. By that behaviour, `NATIVE_DIR=~/metis-run` (one level too high on this machine) deletes lanes/ and snaps/, which hold the cleanup that is not merged back into the repo yet, and a relative `NATIVE_DIR=../..` run from apps/metis resolves against the app and empties the repo root, .git and apps/ included; the repo has no commit yet, so git cannot bring anything back. This is the only gate that deletes outside the app, and `pnpm verify` runs it on every Mac.
- Fix: before the rsync, resolve NATIVE_DIR to an absolute path and refuse a target that equals or contains the app or the home folder; when the target exists and is not empty, require a marker the gate writes on first use (for example `.metis-native-gate`), else exit 1 with "NATIVE_DIR <path> is not empty and was not made by gate:native". Add the three cases to the native-gate tests.
- approach-changing: no, a guard of a few lines before :150
- trigger: a developer sets `NATIVE_DIR=~/metis-run` or `NATIVE_DIR=../..` and runs `pnpm gate:native` or `pnpm verify`; rsync deletes every non-excluded file in that folder before any build step starts
- guard-bypass: :148 only creates the folder and :153 only compares the stamp after the copy, so nothing looks at the target before rsync; the gate's tests run it with a fake sh (scripts/native-gate.run.test.mjs:104,116), so no test executes a real rsync
- design: yes, a target check with a marker file

🟡 major  The lint rule for typed UI text misses a literal one level down (conditional, logical, concatenation), a literal held in a const, other naming attributes, and every sentence in a model file
- key: eslint-rules/restrictions.js#ui-text-holes
- Where: eslint-rules/restrictions.js:28-35 (the selectors reach a literal only as the direct child of the JSX expression container, :32 and :34); eslint.config.js:35,78 (uiText applies to *.tsx only) and :80 (model files get no uiText); CONTRIBUTING.md:166-169; src/shell/model.ts:9
- Why: Measured with eslint --stdin as src/shell/ProbeText.tsx from the lane (config equal to the snapshot by cmp): of 8 typed-text shapes, 2 were flagged (a template child and plain JSX text). These 6 passed: `<Text>{open ? 'Open menu' : 'Closed'}</Text>`, `<Text>{count === 0 && 'No items'}</Text>`, `<Text>{'Items: ' + count}</Text>`, `aria-label={open ? 'Close menu' : 'Open menu'}`, `aria-label={CLOSE}` with a module const, and `aria-description="Opens the menu"`. A model file holding `{ label: 'Close menu', title: 'Not built yet' }` (as src/shell/model.probe.ts) passed with exit 0, yet model files are where the shell composes all its text (model.ts:9). A toggle's label is the usual case for the first shape, and CONTRIBUTING.md:166-169 tells the agency that lint rejects typed text in these places.
- Fix: in restrictions.js add, for the NAMED_BY attributes and for the JSX child position, `JSXExpressionContainer > :matches(ConditionalExpression, LogicalExpression, BinaryExpression) > :matches(${STRING}, TemplateLiteral)`; add `aria-description` and `aria-valuetext` to NAMED_BY; and add a block for `src/**/model{,.*}.ts` that rejects a string literal holding a space (`Literal[value=/\\s/]`). Measured false positives over shipped src: 0 NAMED_BY attributes with a literal branch (the one conditional, src/design-system/Avatar.tsx:23, has `undefined` and `name`), 0 JSX children with a string branch, and 0 single-quoted word-space-word literals in the non-test model files.
- approach-changing: no, selectors and one config block
- trigger: a plan C toggle in src/shell or src/screens writes `aria-label={open ? 'Close filters' : 'Open filters'}`, or a model returns `label: 'No items'`; gate:lint passes, and the Vietnamese page and its screen reader announce English
- guard-bypass: esquery's `>` stops at the ConditionalExpression, LogicalExpression or BinaryExpression between the container and the literal; a const is an Identifier; model files are .ts and the uiText block covers .tsx only; the dictionary audit (src/core/i18n/audit.ts) reads dictionaries, never component or model code

🟡 major  Demo names are still typed in two or three fixture modules, so renaming the demo client changes three files and a one-sided rename passes every test
- key: src/mocks/fixtures#names-restated-across-fixtures
- Where: 12 distinctive values defined in more than one fixture file (a scan of the fixture literals with no-restated-literals' own distinctiveness test), for example 'Northwind Furniture Co.' at src/mocks/fixtures/meridian.ts:11, shell.ts:51 and showroom.ts:11; 'Meridian CGI Campaign' at meridian.ts:10 and shell.ts:53; 'Northwind Showroom VR' at showroom.ts:10 and shell.ts:54; 'Nadia R.' at shell.ts:36 and meridian.ts:12,54; 'Denny K.' and 'denny-k' at meridian.ts:53 and showroom.ts:12,42
- Why: CONTRIBUTING.md:55-56 says renaming the demo client must change one file, and 'Northwind Furniture Co.' is the literal the owner named when he flagged duplication. The cleanup gave ids one home (IDS) but left in each module the names that tie the shell tree to the overview fixtures. A rename in shell.ts alone makes the sidebar tree and the breadcrumb (src/shell/model.ts:55-62) name the project and the client one way while the project header (meridian.ts:10-11) names them another, and every test stays green because each one reads the fixture it renders.
- Fix: give each shared fact one home: build shell.ts's tree names from the overview fixtures (`name: meridian.project.name`, the program's `name: meridian.project.client`), take the PM, the workload people and the shell user from one `PEOPLE` export beside IDS (`{ nadia: { name: 'Nadia R.', initials: 'NR', id: 'nadia-r' }, ... }`). Values equal by chance, such as the category names 'Deliverables' and 'Timeline', may stay.
- approach-changing: no, imports between fixture modules
- trigger: someone renames the demo client in src/mocks/fixtures/shell.ts:51 only; the sidebar's program row and the breadcrumb show the new name, the overview header still shows 'Northwind Furniture Co.', and gate:unit, gate:web and check-web-release all pass
- guard-bypass: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js:71,85 returns early for any file that is not a test, so a fixture restating another fixture is never reported; its table (:46-49) records both files for such a value but uses them only in the message it gives a test
- design: yes, a shared names and people export the fixtures import

💭 nit  HOME is a shortcut that ships the demo ids in the release bundle, written without the `ponytail:` marker the conventions require
- key: src/platform/config.ts#home-shortcut-unmarked
- Where: src/platform/config.ts:9-10; src/app/index.tsx:8; src/shell/workspace.tsx:34; scripts/check-web-release.mjs:29; CONTRIBUTING.md:43
- Why: config.ts:9 says HOME holds "until the back end returns the user's default workspace", so it is a deliberate ceiling, but it lacks the `ponytail: <ceiling>; <how to lift it>` marker CONTRIBUTING.md:43 asks of every shortcut (4 other shipped lines carry one, by grep), so a search for open shortcuts misses it. Its effect: a release build opens /w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview on a cold start, and check-web-release.mjs:29 has to drop both ids from its markers because shipped code holds them. The ids cannot drift from the fixtures (src/platform/config.test.ts:16-18), so this is about tracking only.
- Fix: at config.ts:9, `// ponytail: a release opens the demo project on a cold start; lift it with the user's default workspace from the API.`
- approach-changing: no, a comment

💭 nit  On iOS and Android the mock layer sends a request no handler answers to the network without a word, where the web logs an error
- key: src/platform/mocks.ts#silent-fallthrough
- Where: src/platform/mocks.ts:13-14 (`?? network(input, init)`); contrast src/platform/mocks.web.ts:15-17
- Why: The cleanup made the web worker print an error for an API request no handler answers (mocks.web.ts:16), but left the native fetch wrapper as it was (diff -u against the round-1 tree: comment lines only). A mock build on a phone that calls an endpoint with no handler yet (the next screen's API) gets a network error from the unresolvable .test host, drawn as "The server did not answer. Try again in a moment." or the menu error, with nothing in the Metro log saying a handler is missing.
- Fix: in `mocked`, when getResponse returns undefined and the request's host is `new URL(apiConfig.baseUrl).host`, call `console.error('[mocks] no handler for', request.method, request.url)` before falling through; import apiConfig from './config' as mocks.web.ts does.
- approach-changing: no
